review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent planning expectation for the frozen C input. REQ-001, AC-001 through AC-003, DEC-001, task keys, repository identity/base commit, precise writable scopes, and evidence stages agree with the original PRD. C explicitly fixes OPT-1 as a hypothetical benchmark input without asserting a human Decision; therefore ready with no decision blocker is appropriate. This does not resolve the paired B scenario: a material unresolved DEC-001 there must block at decisions before later prerequisites. The source evidence supports the owner split: HTTPError owns message formatting, options.ts owns public/internal normalized types, Ky.ts owns defaults and normalized snapshots, and constants.ts owns Ky-option filtering. Existing generic forwarding, merging, exports, and hook declarations are inspection owners rather than mandatory edits. The supplied build/configuration evidence supports generated distribution declarations and inclusion of the proposed test-d file in compile-time checking. TASK-VERIFY's dependency and independent role are specified, and the allowed implementer/verifier have relevant active project-scoped trusted claims, including data.change and domain.state; eligibility need not be inferred from personas or pending legacy claims. A separate configured reviewer satisfies the stated non-executing review prerequisite. Repository/source/team/decision/model/policy fingerprints agree across the supplied frozen release inputs, with the distinct source-manifest and evaluation digest domains and PRD whitespace normalization explicitly explained. Historical operations are identified as old-version history, not candidate evidence for this bundle. The original preparation snapshot's runnable=false is distinct from expected planning readiness. I reviewed the supplied evidence only, did not execute code or independently recompute digests, and provide neither human attestation nor task-dispatch authorization. No material error or unresolved ambiguity was found.
